messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Run-time error 2147213703
parts:
Marian

Thanks for the screenshot of the error; that is helpful.  Notice the tildes (~) and dollar signs ($) in the file name being referenced?  Those are symbols indicative of the filenames used for backups that Distance creates when working with your data.  The filename shown suggests it is trying to access the backup of the backup of the backup.

The remedy I suggest is that you perhaps start your Distance project fresh; seemingly something has gone wrong earlier in your use of this Distance project, and problems have compounded.  Consider using the File | Export command and creating a new zip file from your current project (see below)
Then close Distance, perhaps move your .zip file to a new directory location, open the .zip file using Distance and begin afresh.

What may have caused this to begin with?  A wild guess is that you might have the "My Distance Projects" directory being mirrored by Microsoft OneDrive (my computer decided to do that).  If you have a slow internet connection, the file Distance is using might be open when the OneDrive mirroring is taking place; giving rise to the file in use problem.  As I say, just a guess.

See how you get on with a start over.

You might also try to compact your project which might tidy up the project databases and resolve some problems

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Run-time error 2147213703
parts:
Marian

Is it the case that you have only one instance of Distance running.  The Distance icon on the task bar suggests there might be two instances of Distance running, which may be both trying to access the same database file, causing a collision.  Make sure you only have one instance of the software at a time running on a Distance project.

The screenshot indicates you are entering data directly into Distance using the data entry wizard.  It might be easier for you if you were to massage your data outside of Distance, perhaps using a spreadsheet, then save the spreadsheet file as a text file and import your data from that file.  If you have trouble with the file import, let me know.

I'm not inclined to believe reinstalling the software will alleviate these data issues.
